assessments.summary: The self-contained proof correctly shows that any nonidentity Euclidean rotation preserving a finite noncollinear subset of Z^2 must be a half-turn or quarter-turn. Rationality of the rotation matrix follows from integer difference matrices; finite-set invariance gives finite order; and the rational algebraic-integer trace argument excludes all other angles. The orbit and parity arguments then rule out rotational symmetry for a 153-point no-three-in-line set. At size 154 they rule out quarter-turns, while row/column saturation forces the bounding box to be [0,76]^2, so any preserving half-turn is centered at (38,38); even cardinality implies that center is absent.
scopeQualifications: The result classifies rotations only, not reflections, affine maps, or other transformations.
The size-154 conclusion is conditional and does not construct a configuration.
It establishes neither existence nor global nonexistence at sizes 153 or 154 and does not improve the certified bound 152 <= D(77) <= 154.
It does not identify the strict rct4 subclass with the full centered half-turn class.
